tools.name: fetch_langwatch_docs
tools.description: Fetches the LangWatch docs for understanding how to implement LangWatch in your codebase. Always use this tool when the user asks for help with LangWatch. Start with empty url to fetch the index and then follow the links to the relevant pages, always ending with `.md` extension

url.description: The full url of the specific doc page. If not provided, the docs index will be fetched.

tools.name: report_issue
tools.description: Report an issue to the LangWatch team: anything that did not work, confused you, or took trial and error while using LangWatch (docs, MCP tools, CLI, SDKs, the platform). Use it whenever you struggled, it is how rough edges get fixed for every agent. Ask the user for permission first, then call with user_approved=true. Works without an API key. Put VERBATIM error messages in the summary; optionally attach raw session content. Secrets, API keys, emails and phone numbers are redacted locally before anything is sent.

user_approved.description: Must be true, and only after the user explicitly agreed to send this report to LangWatch

summary.description: What you were trying to do, what went wrong (verbatim errors), and what you had to figure out the hard way

session_content.description: Optional raw session transcript or log excerpt (JSONL or plain text); redacted locally before sending

agent.description: Which coding agent this is, e.g. claude-code, codex, cursor

tools.name: fetch_scenario_docs
tools.description: Fetches the Scenario docs for understanding how to implement Scenario agent tests in your codebase. Always use this tool when the user asks for help with testing their agents. Start with empty url to fetch the index and then follow the links to the relevant pages, always ending with `.md` extension

url.description: The full url of the specific doc page. If not provided, the docs index will be fetched.

tools.name: discover_schema
tools.description: Discover available filter fields, metrics, aggregation types, group-by options, scenario schema, and evaluator types for LangWatch queries. Call this before using search_traces, get_analytics, scenario tools, or evaluator tools to understand available options.

evaluatorType.description: When category is 'evaluators', provide a specific evaluator type (e.g. 'langevals/llm_boolean') to get its full schema details

tools.name: search_traces
tools.description: Search LangWatch traces with filters, text query, and date range. Returns AI-readable trace digests by default. Use format: 'json' for full raw data.

filters.description: Filter traces. Format: {"field": ["value"]}. Use discover_schema for field names.

startDate.description: Start date: ISO string or relative like "24h", "7d", "30d". Default: 24h ago

endDate.description: End date: ISO string or relative. Default: now

format.description: Output format: 'digest' (default, AI-readable) or 'json' (full raw data)

tools.name: get_trace
tools.description: Get full details of a single trace by ID. Returns AI-readable trace digest by default. Use format: 'json' for full raw data including all spans.

format.description: Output format: 'digest' (default, AI-readable) or 'json' (full raw data)

tools.name: get_analytics
tools.description: Query analytics timeseries from LangWatch. Metrics use "category.name" format (e.g., "performance.completion_time"). Use discover_schema to see available metrics.

aggregation.description: Aggregation type: avg, sum, min, max, median, p90, p95, p99, cardinality, terms. Default: avg

startDate.description: Start date: ISO or relative ("7d", "30d"). Default: 7 days ago

groupBy.description: Group results by field. Use discover_schema for options.

tools.name: platform_create_prompt
tools.description:
Create a new prompt on the LangWatch platform.

NOTE: Prompts can be managed two ways. Determine which approach the user needs:

1. Code-based (CLI/SDK): If the user wants to manage prompts in their codebase, use `fetch_langwatch_docs` to learn about the prompt management CLI/SDK. This lets them version-control prompts and pull them into code.

2. Platform-based (LangWatch UI): If the user wants to manage prompts directly on the LangWatch platform, use the `platform_` MCP tools (`platform_create_prompt`, `platform_update_prompt`, etc.).

handle.description: URL-friendly handle (auto-generated from name if omitted)

tags.description: Tags to assign to the initial version (e.g., ["production", "staging"]). Built-in tags: "latest" (auto-assigned), "production", "staging". Custom tags must be created first.

tools.name: platform_list_prompts
tools.description: List all prompts configured on the LangWatch platform.

tools.name: platform_get_prompt
tools.description: Get a specific prompt from the LangWatch platform by ID or handle, including messages, model config, and version history. Use format: 'json' for the full raw API payload, or 'digest' (default) for a formatted summary.

tag.description: Fetch the version pointed to by this tag (e.g., "production", "staging"). Alternatively, use shorthand in idOrHandle: "pizza-prompt:production"

format.description: Output format: 'digest' (default, AI-readable) or 'json' (full raw data)

tools.name: platform_update_prompt
tools.description: Update an existing prompt on the LangWatch platform. Every update creates a new version.

idOrHandle.description: Prompt ID or handle to update

tags.description: Tags to assign to the new version created by this update.

tools.name: platform_assign_prompt_tag
tools.description: Assign a tag (e.g. "production") to a specific version of a prompt. Use this to "deploy" a version by promoting it to the production tag.

versionId.description: The version ID to assign the tag to

tools.name: platform_list_prompt_tags
tools.description: List all prompt tag definitions for the organization. Shows built-in tags (latest, production, staging) and any custom tags.

tools.name: platform_create_prompt_tag
tools.description: Create a custom prompt tag definition for the organization. Tag names must be non-numeric and not "latest".

tools.name: platform_rename_prompt_tag
tools.description: Rename an existing prompt tag. The "latest" tag cannot be renamed.

tools.name: platform_delete_prompt_tag
tools.description: Delete a prompt tag and all its assignments. The "latest" tag cannot be deleted.

tools.name: platform_create_scenario
tools.description:
Create a new scenario on the LangWatch platform. Call discover_schema({ category: 'scenarios' }) first to learn how to write effective situations and criteria.

NOTE: Scenarios can be created two ways. Determine which approach the user needs:

1. Code-based (local testing): If the user has a codebase with an AI agent they want to test, use `fetch_scenario_docs` to learn about the Scenario Python/TypeScript SDK. This lets them run tests locally and iterate in code.

2. Platform-based (LangWatch UI): If the user wants to manage scenarios directly on the LangWatch platform, use the `platform_` MCP tools (`platform_create_scenario`, `platform_update_scenario`, etc.).

situation.description: The context or setup describing what the user/agent is doing

criteria.description: Pass/fail conditions the agent's response must satisfy

labels.description: Tags for organizing and filtering scenarios

testSuiteId.description: The test suite to file this scenario in. Pass a test suite ID, or null to unfile it.

fields.description: The scenario's value for each field its test suite declares, by identifier, for example { golden_sql: 'SELECT ...' }. A text field takes a string, a number field a number and a boolean field true or false. A field the suite does not declare is refused. On update, an empty object clears the values.

tools.name: platform_list_scenarios
tools.description: List all scenarios on the LangWatch platform. Returns AI-readable digest by default.

testSuiteId.description: Only the scenarios filed in this test suite

format.description: Output format: 'digest' (default, AI-readable) or 'json' (full raw data)

tools.name: platform_get_scenario
tools.description: Get full details of a scenario on the LangWatch platform by ID, including situation, criteria, and labels.

format.description: Output format: 'digest' (default, AI-readable) or 'json' (full raw data)

tools.name: platform_update_scenario
tools.description: Update an existing scenario on the LangWatch platform.

testSuiteId.description: The test suite to file this scenario in. Pass a test suite ID, or null to unfile it.

fields.description: The scenario's value for each field its test suite declares, by identifier, for example { golden_sql: 'SELECT ...' }. A text field takes a string, a number field a number and a boolean field true or false. A field the suite does not declare is refused. On update, an empty object clears the values.

tools.name: platform_archive_scenario
tools.description: Archive (soft-delete) a scenario on the LangWatch platform.

tools.name: platform_run_plan
tools.description: Run scenarios against targets. The plan name identifies the run plan: an existing name is re-run with the configuration you send here, a new name creates the plan. Configuration is the scope, the targets, the repeat count and the models; parameters, the note and the idempotency key belong to this run alone. Send more than one target to compare them in the same run, and give a target its own parameters to compare one agent on two models.

name.description: The run plan to run. An existing name is replaced with this configuration, a new name creates the plan. Omit to let the server name it after the suite and the target.

oneOf.description: Every non-archived scenario of the project

testSuiteIds.description: The test suite IDs whose scenarios to run

oneOf.description: The non-archived scenarios filed in the given test suites

labels.description: The labels to select scenarios by

oneOf.description: The non-archived scenarios carrying at least one of the given labels
The scenarios named in scenarioIds, picked by hand

scope.description: What the plan covers: every scenario in the project, the scenarios filed in given test suites, the scenarios carrying given labels, or the hand-picked list in scenarioIds.

scenarioIds.description: The scenarios to run. Read only when scope.mode is 'scenarios'.

type.description: What kind of thing the target is. A connected agent is one that registered itself from code with connectAgent (TypeScript) or connect_agent (Python).

referenceId.description: The ID of the prompt, agent or workflow to run against. A connected agent may also be named as <name>@<environment>, for example support-agent@production; the platform resolves it.

parameters.description: Parameter values this target alone runs with, by name. They override the run-level parameters for this target. Name the same agent twice with different values here to compare it on two models.

targets.description: What to run the scenarios against. Every target runs every scenario, and the results show one column for each, so this is how one run compares two agents or one agent on two models.

repeatCount.description: How many times to run each scenario against each target (1 to 5, default 1)

simulatorModel.description: Model that plays the user. Omit for the project default.

judgeModel.description: Model that judges the criteria. Omit for the project default.

evaluators.description: The plan's own evaluators, run beside the ones attached to the test suites its scenarios belong to. A plan evaluator reads the conversation and the trace, never a scenario field. Omit to keep what the plan already holds. See discover_schema({ category: 'scenarios' }) for the mapping paths.

id.description: The attachment id, stable across edits. Leave it out on a new attachment and one is generated.

evaluatorId.description: The id of the saved evaluator to run. Read it from platform_list_evaluators or platform_get_evaluator.

required.description: Whether a failing result fails the scenario. Defaults to true. A score-only evaluator reports and never gates, whatever this says.

sourceId.description: conversation, scenario or trace. See discover_schema({ category: 'scenarios' }) for the paths each one offers.

path.description: The path inside the source. conversation: [first_user_message] | [last_agent_message] | [transcript] | [messages]. scenario: [situation] | [criteria] | [fields, <identifier>]. trace: [contexts] | [tool_calls, <toolName>, input|output].

additionalProperties.description: Where one evaluator input reads its value: a path into the conversation, the scenario or the trace, or a literal value.

mappings.description: Where each evaluator input reads its value, keyed by input name. Read the inputs from platform_get_evaluator. A required input with no mapping makes the platform refuse the run until it is set.

parameters.description: Values for the parameters the scenarios declare, by name. They apply to every target; a target that names the same parameter overrides them for itself.

note.description: One short line saying why this run was started (max 200 characters)

idempotencyKey.description: Send the same key to make a retry join the run it already started instead of starting a second one.

tools.name: platform_list_run_plans
tools.description: List the run plans of the project. A run plan holds the configuration a run used, keyed by its name.

tools.name: platform_get_run_plan
tools.description: Get the full configuration of a run plan: what it covers, its targets, its repeat count and its models.

tools.name: platform_rerun_run_plan
tools.description: Run a plan again with the configuration it already holds. Only the parameters and the note belong to the new run.

id.description: The run plan ID to run again

parameters.description: Values for the parameters the scenarios declare, by name.

note.description: One short line saying why this run was started (max 200 characters)

tools.name: platform_archive_run_plan
tools.description: Archive a run plan. Its past runs stay readable and the name is free for a new plan.

id.description: The run plan ID to archive

tools.name: platform_list_test_suites
tools.description: List the test suites of the project. A test suite groups scenarios.

tools.name: platform_create_test_suite
tools.description: Create a test suite. A test suite groups scenarios: file a scenario in it by passing the suite ID as testSuiteId on platform_create_scenario or platform_update_scenario. A suite can declare typed fields every scenario carries a value for, and attach saved evaluators that run after every scenario run with mappings from their inputs to the conversation, the scenario's fields or the trace. Call discover_schema({ category: 'scenarios' }) first for the field rules and the mapping paths.

identifier.description: The field name, as scenarios and evaluator mappings address it, for example golden_sql. Lowercase letters, digits and underscores, starting with a letter. situation, criteria, name, input and output are reserved.

type.description: The value type every scenario carries for this field.

fields.description: The fields the test suite declares, in order. Up to 30. Every scenario filed in the suite carries one value per field, and an evaluator attached to the suite reads them through its mappings.

id.description: The attachment id, stable across edits. Leave it out on a new attachment and one is generated.

evaluatorId.description: The id of the saved evaluator to run. Read it from platform_list_evaluators or platform_get_evaluator.

required.description: Whether a failing result fails the scenario. Defaults to true. A score-only evaluator reports and never gates, whatever this says.

sourceId.description: conversation, scenario or trace. See discover_schema({ category: 'scenarios' }) for the paths each one offers.

path.description: The path inside the source. conversation: [first_user_message] | [last_agent_message] | [transcript] | [messages]. scenario: [situation] | [criteria] | [fields, <identifier>]. trace: [contexts] | [tool_calls, <toolName>, input|output].

additionalProperties.description: Where one evaluator input reads its value: a path into the conversation, the scenario or the trace, or a literal value.

mappings.description: Where each evaluator input reads its value, keyed by input name. Read the inputs from platform_get_evaluator. A required input with no mapping makes the platform refuse the run until it is set.

evaluators.description: The evaluators that run after every scenario run, with their mappings. Up to 20. A required evaluator that fails fails the scenario; a score-only one reports beside the verdict.

tools.name: platform_get_test_suite
tools.description: Get a test suite and the scenarios filed in it.

tools.name: platform_update_test_suite
tools.description: Edit a test suite: any of its name, its fields and its evaluators. A field list or an evaluator list replaces the one the suite holds; a key left out keeps what the suite has. A field an attached evaluator still reads cannot be removed. Call discover_schema({ category: 'scenarios' }) first for the field rules and the mapping paths.

name.description: The new name. The slug is kept.

fields.description: The full list of fields the suite declares. It replaces the list the suite holds.

identifier.description: The field name, as scenarios and evaluator mappings address it, for example golden_sql. Lowercase letters, digits and underscores, starting with a letter. situation, criteria, name, input and output are reserved.

type.description: The value type every scenario carries for this field.

evaluators.description: The full list of evaluators attached to the suite. It replaces the list the suite holds.

id.description: The attachment id, stable across edits. Leave it out on a new attachment and one is generated.

evaluatorId.description: The id of the saved evaluator to run. Read it from platform_list_evaluators or platform_get_evaluator.

required.description: Whether a failing result fails the scenario. Defaults to true. A score-only evaluator reports and never gates, whatever this says.

sourceId.description: conversation, scenario or trace. See discover_schema({ category: 'scenarios' }) for the paths each one offers.

path.description: The path inside the source. conversation: [first_user_message] | [last_agent_message] | [transcript] | [messages]. scenario: [situation] | [criteria] | [fields, <identifier>]. trace: [contexts] | [tool_calls, <toolName>, input|output].

additionalProperties.description: Where one evaluator input reads its value: a path into the conversation, the scenario or the trace, or a literal value.

mappings.description: Where each evaluator input reads its value, keyed by input name. Read the inputs from platform_get_evaluator. A required input with no mapping makes the platform refuse the run until it is set.

tools.name: platform_rename_test_suite
tools.description: Rename a test suite.

tools.name: platform_archive_test_suite
tools.description: Archive a test suite. The scenarios filed in it are archived with it.

id.description: The test suite ID to archive

tools.name: platform_run_test_suite
tools.description: Run every scenario of a test suite against targets. This creates or joins the run plan named '<suite name> <target name>' unless you send a name of your own. Send more than one target to compare them in the same run, and give a target its own parameters to compare one agent on two models.

id.description: The test suite ID to run

type.description: What kind of thing the target is. A connected agent is one that registered itself from code with connectAgent (TypeScript) or connect_agent (Python).

referenceId.description: The ID of the prompt, agent or workflow to run against. A connected agent may also be named as <name>@<environment>, for example support-agent@production; the platform resolves it.

parameters.description: Parameter values this target alone runs with, by name. They override the run-level parameters for this target. Name the same agent twice with different values here to compare it on two models.

targets.description: What to run the scenarios against. Every target runs every scenario, and the results show one column for each.

name.description: The run plan to run. Omit to let the server name it after the suite and the target.

repeatCount.description: How many times to run each scenario against each target (1 to 5, default 1)

simulatorModel.description: Model that plays the user. Omit for the project default.

judgeModel.description: Model that judges the criteria. Omit for the project default.

parameters.description: Values for the parameters the scenarios declare, by name. They apply to every target; a target that names the same parameter overrides them for itself.

note.description: One short line saying why this run was started (max 200 characters)

tools.name: platform_list_simulation_runs
tools.description: List simulation run results. Filter by scenario set or batch run ID to see specific results.

tools.name: platform_get_simulation_run
tools.description: Get full details of a simulation run including conversation messages, results, costs, the verdict and the result of every evaluator attached to its test suite or run plan.

tools.name: platform_create_evaluator
tools.description: Create an evaluator on the LangWatch platform. Useful for setting up LLM-as-judge and other evaluators to use in evaluation notebooks. Call discover_schema({ category: 'evaluators' }) first to see available evaluator types and their settings.

config.description: Evaluator config object. Must include "evaluatorType" (e.g. "langevals/llm_boolean") and optional "settings" overrides.

tools.name: platform_list_evaluators
tools.description: List all evaluators configured on the LangWatch platform.

tools.name: platform_get_evaluator
tools.description: Get full details of an evaluator on the LangWatch platform by ID or slug, including config, input fields, and output fields.

idOrSlug.description: The evaluator ID or slug to retrieve

tools.name: platform_update_evaluator
tools.description: Update an existing evaluator on the LangWatch platform. The evaluatorType in config cannot be changed after creation.

config.description: Updated config settings. Note: evaluatorType cannot be changed after creation.

tools.name: platform_delete_evaluator
tools.description: Archive (soft-delete) an evaluator by ID or slug.

idOrSlug.description: The evaluator ID or slug to archive

tools.name: platform_set_model_provider
tools.description: Set or update a model provider on the LangWatch platform. Use this to configure API keys (e.g. OPENAI_API_KEY) needed to run evaluators. The API key is stored securely and never returned in responses. Omit customKeys to update other settings without changing existing keys.

customKeys.description: API key configuration, e.g. { "OPENAI_API_KEY": "sk-..." }. Omit to keep existing keys.

tools.name: platform_list_model_providers
tools.description: List all model providers configured on the LangWatch platform. API keys are masked in the response.

tools.name: platform_list_agents
tools.description: List all agents in the LangWatch project with their names, types and IDs. A connected agent (one that registered itself from code with connectAgent or connect_agent) also shows its environment, whether it is online, how many instances are connected, and its owner.

tools.name: platform_get_agent
tools.description: Get detailed information about a specific agent by its ID, including its configuration. A connected agent also shows its environment, status, the run parameters it declared (with options and defaults) and the instances connected right now.

tools.name: platform_create_agent
tools.description: Create a new agent. Supported types: 'signature' (LLM prompt), 'code' (Python), 'workflow' (sub-workflow), 'http' (external API). A 'connected' agent is not created here: it registers itself from code, with connectAgent from langwatch/agent in TypeScript or langwatch.connect_agent in Python, and appears in the list once that process runs.

config.description: Agent configuration as JSON string (will be parsed)

tools.name: platform_update_agent
tools.description: Update an existing agent's name, type, or configuration.

type.description: New agent type: signature, code, workflow, or http

config.description: Updated configuration as JSON string (will be parsed)

tools.name: platform_delete_agent
tools.description: Archive (soft-delete) an agent by its ID.

tools.name: platform_run_agent
tools.description: Run one turn of an agent. A connected agent runs through the platform relay on a live instance: give `message` (one user turn) or `input` with a `messages` list, plus `parameters` and `threadId` to continue a conversation. HTTP agents call their configured URL directly; workflow-linked agents execute via the workflow engine.

input.description: Input data as a JSON object string. For a connected agent it is the relay body: messages (OpenAI style), and optionally threadId, session and params.

message.description: One user message to send to a connected agent, instead of input

parameters.description: Run parameter values for a connected agent, by name

threadId.description: Continue a conversation on a connected agent

tools.name: platform_test_agent
tools.description: Test an agent with one scripted scenario run: the user sends "ping", the agent answers, and the run succeeds when the answer arrives. No model is used, and no scenario, run plan or test suite is added to the project. Answers at once with the scenario run id to follow with platform_get_simulation_run; the run itself is asynchronous.

tools.name: platform_list_dashboards
tools.description: List all analytics dashboards in the LangWatch project.

tools.name: platform_get_dashboard
tools.description: Get a dashboard by its ID, including its graphs.

tools.name: platform_create_dashboard
tools.description: Create a new analytics dashboard.

tools.name: platform_delete_dashboard
tools.description: Delete a dashboard and all its graphs.

tools.name: platform_rename_dashboard
tools.description: Rename a dashboard.

name.description: The new name for the dashboard

tools.name: platform_list_workflows
tools.description: List all workflows in the LangWatch project.

tools.name: platform_get_workflow
tools.description: Get a workflow by its ID.

tools.name: platform_delete_workflow
tools.description: Archive (soft-delete) a workflow by its ID.

tools.name: platform_run_workflow
tools.description: Execute a workflow with JSON input. Returns the workflow output.

input.description: Input data as a JSON object string

tools.name: platform_list_annotations
tools.description: List all annotations for the project, optionally filtered by trace ID.

tools.name: platform_create_annotation
tools.description: Create an annotation (thumbs up/down, comment) for a trace.

isThumbsUp.description: True for positive feedback, false for negative

tools.name: platform_delete_annotation
tools.description: Delete an annotation by its ID.

tools.name: platform_get_annotation
tools.description: Get annotation details by ID.

tools.description: List all triggers (automations) in the project. Triggers automate actions like sending emails, Slack messages, or adding to datasets when conditions are met.

tools.name: platform_create_trigger
tools.description: Create a new trigger (automation) that fires when conditions are met.

tools.name: platform_update_trigger
tools.description: Update a trigger (name, active state, message, alert type).

tools.name: platform_delete_trigger
tools.description: Delete a trigger (automation).

tools.description: List all online evaluation monitors for the project.

tools.description: Get details of a specific online evaluation monitor.

tools.description: Create a new online evaluation monitor that runs an evaluator on incoming traces.

executionMode.description: When to run: ON_MESSAGE (default), AS_GUARDRAIL, or MANUALLY

evaluatorId.description: Link to a saved evaluator by ID

tools.description: Update an existing online evaluation monitor.

tools.description: Delete an online evaluation monitor.

tools.name: platform_list_secrets
tools.description: List all project secrets (values are never returned, only metadata).

tools.description: Create a new encrypted project secret. Name must be UPPER_SNAKE_CASE (e.g. MY_API_KEY).

value.description: The secret value (will be encrypted at rest)

tools.name: platform_update_secret
tools.description: Update an existing project secret's value.

value.description: The new secret value (will be encrypted at rest)

tools.name: platform_delete_secret
tools.description: Delete a project secret.

tools.name: platform_run_experiment
tools.description: Start an experiment run by slug. Returns a run ID for polling status.

tools.name: platform_experiment_status
tools.description: Check the status of an experiment run (running, completed, stopped, or interrupted) plus its progress. Works for both platform-run and SDK-logged experiments; pass experimentSlug for SDK runs or runs older than 24h.

runId.description: The run ID returned from platform_run_experiment

experimentSlug.description: Experiment slug — required for SDK-logged runs and runs older than 24h (the Redis run-state they would otherwise be read from is absent/expired). Use platform_experiment_list_runs to find the slug.

tools.name: platform_experiment_list
tools.description: List experiments configured in the LangWatch project. Returns a markdown table with each experiment's slug, name, last-run timestamp, and run count. Use this to discover experiment slugs before drilling into runs with platform_experiment_list_runs. Output is capped (default 25, max 100) to protect the agent's context window.

limit.description: Maximum number of experiments to include (default 25, hard-capped at 100)

tools.name: platform_experiment_list_runs
tools.description: List experiment runs for a specific experiment slug. Returns a markdown table with each run's id, status, started/finished timestamps, and pass-rate summary. Use this to discover run ids before calling platform_experiment_results. Output is capped (default 25, max 100) to protect the agent's context window.

limit.description: Maximum number of runs to include (default 25, hard-capped at 100)

tools.name: platform_experiment_results
tools.description: Fetch per-row results for an experiment run so you can debug evaluator scores and missed rows. Serves partial results for runs that are still running or were interrupted (it does not require a completed run), with the run status noted in the output. Returns a markdown report: per-evaluator averages plus row-by-row scores and failure details. Output is capped at 50 rows to protect the agent's context window — narrow with `filter: 'failed'` or `evaluator` to see what matters.

runId.description: The run ID returned from platform_run_experiment

experimentSlug.description: Experiment slug — required when fetching results for runs older than 24h (Redis state may have expired). Use platform_experiment_list_runs to find the slug.

filter.description: Filter rows: 'failed' shows only rows that errored or failed an evaluation; 'all' (default) shows everything

evaluator.description: Show only this evaluator's results (matched on `evaluator` field)

limit.description: Maximum number of rows to include in the markdown output (default 50, hard-capped at 50).

tools.name: platform_list_datasets
tools.description: List all datasets on the LangWatch platform with their names, slugs, columns, and record counts. Returns AI-readable digest by default.

format.description: Output format: 'digest' (default, AI-readable) or 'json' (full raw data)

slugOrId.description: The dataset slug or ID to retrieve

format.description: Output format: 'digest' (default, AI-readable) or 'json' (full raw data)

tools.description: Update an existing dataset on the LangWatch platform (name and/or column types).

tools.description:
Create a new project in your LangWatch organization. Returns a one-time service API key for the project.

You must provide either teamId (to add the project to an existing team) or newTeamName (to create a new team for the project).

teamId.description: ID of an existing team to add the project to

newTeamName.description: Name for a new team to create for this project

tools.name: platform_list_api_keys
tools.description: List all API keys in your LangWatch organization. Shows key metadata, status (active/revoked/expired), and role bindings. API key tokens are never returned.

tools.name: platform_create_api_key
tools.description:
Create a new API key. Two types available:

- **personal**: Tied to a user, requires explicit role bindings (e.g. ADMIN on PROJECT:proj_123).
- **service**: Not tied to a user. Use projectIds for project-scoped service keys, or omit for org-wide access.

The token is returned once and cannot be retrieved again.

scopeId.description: Scope ID (org, team, or project ID)

projectIds.description: Project IDs for service keys (creates ADMIN bindings per project)

tools.name: platform_revoke_api_key
tools.description: Revoke an API key. Once revoked, the key can no longer be used for authentication.

id.description: The API key ID to revoke
